title: Formal exponential does not decrease the convergence radius
statement:
Let $U(T)=\sum_{n\ge1}u_nT^n\in T\mathbf C[[T]]$ be a complex formal power series with constant coefficient zero [def-weil-formal-power-series]. Form its formal exponential
$$E(T)=\exp(U(T))=\sum_{r\ge0}\frac{U(T)^r}{r!}$$
with the coefficientwise finite convention of [def-weil-power-series-exponential]. Let $R(U),R(E)\in[0,\infty]$ be the absolute convergence radii of [d-real-series]. Then
$$R(E)\ge R(U).$$

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: "The assumed energy bound makes the series in the exponential converge ... Its analytic exponential is holomorphic there and agrees with the rational germ." General scalar convergence input.

proof.text: Fix a real $\rho\ge0$ for which $\sum_{n\ge1}|u_n|t^n$ converges for every $0\le t<\rho$, as in [d-real-series]. Fix any such $t$, and put $a_0=0$ and $a_n=|u_n|t^n$ for $n\ge1$. This is a summable nonnegative real sequence. Let $S$ be its sum. Clause (i) of [lem-dl-a1-nonnegative-series-partial-sums] gives $\sum_{j=1}^{N}a_j\le S$ for every $N$, and $S\ge0$ by applying it to the empty finite subset.

source.place: Last paragraph, convergence of the exponent series: choose an admissible disk and a nonnegative scalar majorant.

proof.text:
Write $E(T)=\sum_{n\ge0}e_nT^n$. By [def-weil-power-series-exponential], $e_0=1$ and its displayed finite coefficient formula gives, for $n\ge1$,
$$|e_n|t^n\le b_n:=\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac1{r!}\sum_{\substack{n_1+\cdots+n_r=n,\ n_j\ge1}}\prod_{j=1}^{r}a_{n_j}.$$
Indeed apply the triangle inequality to the finite sums, use $|\prod u_{n_j}|=\prod|u_{n_j}|$ from [def-weil-complex-absolute-value], and replace $t^n$ by $\prod t^{n_j}$. Set $b_0=1$. All terms in these finite real sums are nonnegative, including at $t=0$.

source.place: Last paragraph, coefficientwise comparison; expand the finite coefficient formula in the cited definition (Finite coefficient formulas, 49_zeta_linear_algebra.tex:114–131).
Last paragraph, finite-sum majorization of the formal exponential; the finite distributive calculation is written out here.

proof.text: By [lem-dl-a1-real-factorial-series-summable], $\sum_{r\ge0}S^r/r!$ is summable. Its terms are nonnegative since $S\ge0$. Let $B$ be its real sum. Clause (i) of [lem-dl-a1-nonnegative-series-partial-sums] bounds every partial sum $\sum_{r=0}^{N}S^r/r!$ by $B$. The preceding finite calculation therefore bounds every nonempty initial partial sum of $\sum_n |e_n|t^n$ by $B$; the empty one is $0\le B$. Clause (ii) of that same node, applied to the nonnegative sequence $n\mapsto |e_n|t^n$, proves its summability.

source.place: Last paragraph, convergence of the exponential series on the same disk; general scalar summability inputs.

proof.text: The argument applies to every $0\le t<\rho$, so every real $\rho\ge0$ admissible in the defining supremum for $R(U)$ is admissible for $R(E)$ in [d-real-series]. Inclusion of these sets gives $R(U)\le R(E)$. The admissible radius $\rho=0$ is vacuous; if $R(U)=0$ the inequality follows from nonnegativity, and if $R(U)=\infty$ the same inclusion makes the admissible radii for $E$ unbounded. No convergence at a boundary point is asserted.

source.place: Last paragraph, conclusion by the defining supremum of radii, including 0 and infinity.

proof_origin.place: Last paragraph: expand the omitted absolute-convergence justification by finite coefficient bounds, without analytic composition or infinite-sum rearrangement.
